high.title: Ibovespa rises with improved investor sentiment and retests 169,000 points; 5 things to know before investing today (11)
high.summary: The Ibovespa is tracking improved global risk sentiment amid new developments in the Middle East conflict, with US pressure for a definitive peace agreement. By 10:10 AM Brasília time, the main Brazilian stock index was up 0.19% at 168,939 points, approaching the psychologically important 169,000 level. The USD/BRL pair moved counter to global dollar strength, falling 0.17% to R$ 5.1640, while the DXY was up 0.12%. Brazilian services volume posted a stronger-than-expected 1.2% month-over-month increase in April (vs. 0.6% expected), recovering from March's 1.1% decline and suggesting economic momentum after a weak Q1. This positive domestic data, combined with geopolitical developments and upcoming US inflation data, is supporting Brazilian assets. For FX traders, the real's outperformance against the dollar despite broader dollar strength indicates improving local fundamentals, though the 169,000 Ibovespa resistance level will be key to watch for equity positioning.

medium.title: Petrobras (PETR4) purchases stake in exploratory block in Campos Basin and expands partnership with Equinor
medium.summary: Petrobras announced it signed a contract with Equinor to acquire a 50% stake in the Itaimbezinho exploratory block in deep waters of the Campos Basin. The consortium will be equally split between Equinor (operator) and Petrobras, with PPSA managing the production-sharing agreement. This strategic partnership reinforces Petrobras' long-term strategy to replenish reserves through exploration of new frontiers and expands synergies in the Campos Basin where both companies already operate joint assets.

medium.title: PINE4 and more: check out small cap stocks recommended by BTG Pactual to invest in June
medium.summary: BTG Pactual updated its small cap portfolio recommendations despite challenging market conditions including Middle East tensions and deteriorating interest rate expectations. The bank highlights Banco Pine (PINE4) among its picks, noting the institution delivered positive Q1 2026 results with net income of R$ 150 million, up 25% from the previous quarter. Analysts expect continued market volatility due to high interest rates, above-target inflation, and electoral uncertainties.

medium.title: For the first time in 3 years, ECB raises interest rates to contain inflation caused by war
medium.summary: The European Central Bank raised interest rates for the first time in almost three years to combat inflation driven by energy costs from the Iran war. Eurozone inflation is already above 3%, well above the ECB's 2% target, while economic growth remains weak. This divergent global monetary policy trend could impact Brazilian Real positioning as investors reassess relative interest rate differentials between major economies and emerging markets like Brazil.
